title: Request/Response Orchestrator for OpenAI ChatCompletions Compatibility
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a lightweight orchestrator service that translates Redwood inference API semantics into OpenAI Chat Completions v1-style request/response shapes. The goal is to allow existing third-party clients and internal migration paths to interoperate with Redwood's streaming, function-calling, and structured-output capabilities without changing client libraries. This ticket covers request shaping, response unwrapping, function/tool call lifecycle mapping, and streaming event synthesis for compatibility-mode endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility endpoint accepts OpenAI Chat Completions payloads and returns syntactically valid ChatCompletions responses for both non-stream and streaming clients

Function/tool calling: when Redwood model triggers a tool call, compatibility endpoint emits OpenAI-style function_call events and finalizes with a message containing tool results consistent with ChatCompletions tool-call flow

Streaming: server-sent events or chunked transfer encodings mirror OpenAI streaming frames (delta/content/function_call) and include metadata for Redwood-specific tokens where unavoidable, with a clear opt-in header to expose internal ids
Structured outputs: JSON schema responses produced by Redwood are surfaced as content in choices[0].message.content with content-type annotations when requested
Telemetry: all compatibility requests produce tracing and token-level cost breakdowns and are tagged as compat-mode in analytics
implementation_notes: Introduce an oa-compat adapter module that lives behind the API gateway; keep transformation logic pure and idempotent

Request shaping rules: map messages[] -> messages[] preserving role normalization (assistant/system/user) and normalize name fields; map max_tokens -> max_tokens with guard rails to prevent unbounded sequences

Streaming implementation: fanout Redwood runtime event stream to an SSE/chunked framing layer that emits 'data: [JSON]\n\n' frames matching OpenAI streaming deltas. Maintain order guarantees and handle reconnection semantics by offering resume tokens in headers

Function calling mapping: Redwood returns structured function call objects (name, arguments, call_id). The adapter must translate to: first emission of function_call delta (name and empty arguments), subsequent deltas appending arguments, and a final assistant message with role "assistant" and content containing the serialized function return per OpenAI expectations

Structured outputs and content-type: when model returns structured JSON output with content-type application/json, include message with content set to JSON string and add a message['content_type'] metadata entry serialized into the 'delta' frames when compat header present

Idempotency and dedup: respect Redwood request-id and map to OpenAI 'request_id' header; implement a small in-memory LRU cache for 1 minute to dedupe retries and preserve idempotent tool-call side-effects at the adapter layer
Security: do not leak internal debug fields by default; require X-Redwood-Compat=1 header to enable compat debug annotations
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Deploy adapter in us-west-2 behind a feature flag; route 1% of traffic from internal SDK tests and accepted legacy clients
Phase 1 (staged): Expand to 10% with strict telemetry and rollback alarms for latency or error delta > 2x baseline
Phase 2 (general availability): Open to customer config; document behavior differences and recommended migration steps
Rollback criteria: error rate increase > 4% or median latency increase > 150ms for compat path over native API
test_plan: Unit tests: mapping rules for 20+ message permutations (roles, names, function_call hints)
Integration tests: end-to-end stream from Redwood runtime to SSE frames validated by a synthetic OpenAI-compatible client
Function-call tests: simulate tool failure, slow-tool responses, and guarantee that compatibility frames reflect partial arguments and eventual tool result
Schema tests: verify choices[*].message schema matches OpenAI examples including indexed choices, finish_reason, and content delta framing
Chaos tests: simulate dropped connections and client resumes to verify resume-token semantics and total-order guarantees
telemetry: Emit compat_mode=true tag in all spans and logs for routed requests
Token-level cost metrics preserved and forwarded as chat.usage token counts in analytics events
Add event 'compat.function_call' with fields: function_name, call_id, duration_ms, outcome (success|error)
Dashboard: compat-endpoint latency by region, error rate, and token-cost variance vs native endpoint
